title: Comic Book Flip
aka: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
story: A collector's shop reprices a rare comic every morning, and you have written down the prices for the past few weeks. Had you bought one copy on some day and sold it for the shop's price on a later day, what is the most you could have made?
You buy before you sell, and only once. If every deal loses money, you would not have bought at all.
task: Write bestFlip(prices). prices[i] is the price on day i. Return the largest value of prices[sell] - prices[buy] over all pairs of days with buy < sell.
If no pair makes a profit, or there are fewer than two days, return 0.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 1 at 22 and sell on day 2 at 41: profit 19. Buying at the lowest price, 18 on day 3, only gets 35 - 18 = 17. The cheapest day is not always the best day to buy.
The price only falls, so every deal loses money. Do not trade: 0.
The highest price is 40 and the lowest 5, but 5 comes after 40. The best real deal is 40 - 12 = 28.

hints: Pretend you sell on day 4 in the first example, at 35. Which earlier day would you want to have bought on, and why?
For any selling day, the best buying day is the cheapest day before it. From the past you need just one number.
Walk the days in order, keeping the lowest price so far. What is the best profit if you sell today?
Keep cheapest (lowest price so far) and best (best profit so far, starting at 0). For each price, first update best with price - cheapest, then update cheapest with price.
bruteForce: Try every buying day with every later selling day and keep the largest difference.
That is about n²/2 pairs: roughly 5 billion for 100,000 days. Each selling day rescans all earlier days for the cheapest, though that answer changes by only one day at a time.

js: * @param {number[]} prices  price on each day, in order
* @return {number} the best profit from one buy then one later sell, or 0

tests.note: rising: buy first day, sell last day
global minimum comes too late to help
new minimum later gives the best deal

js: let cheapest = Infinity; // lowest price on any earlier day
let best = 0;            // not trading is always allowed
best = Math.max(best, price - cheapest); // sell today
cheapest = Math.min(cheapest, price);    // or remember today as a buy
py: cheapest = float("inf")  # lowest price on any earlier day
best = 0                 # not trading is always allowed
best = max(best, price - cheapest)  # sell today
cheapest = min(cheapest, price)     # or remember today as a buy
walkthrough: Instead of "which pair of days?", ask for each day: "if I sell today, what is my best profit?" It is today's price minus the cheapest price before today. Carry that cheapest price along and each day costs one step.
• Day 0, 30: nothing to buy from yet. cheapest = 30, best = 0.
Update best before cheapest. The other order lets you buy and sell on the same day: harmless here (profit 0), but a bug in problems where it is not.
solution.timeWhy: One pass, with constant work per day.
solution.spaceWhy: Two numbers, however many days there are.
solution.takeaway: When the best pair is "something earlier, then something later", walk once and carry a summary of the past (here the running minimum). Compare each element with that summary instead of with every earlier element.
